The rubric-level runbook `memory-recall-health` points at via `methodRef`. This
rubric grades the SYSTEM half of recall quality from its own telemetry; the
agent half is `su-agent-behavior`'s `recall-utilization` (see its runbook). The
deterministic teeth are in Vitest — this page is the LIVE read layer.

## Surface liveness (criterion: per-surface-telemetry-liveness)

```sql
SELECT surface, count(*) AS n,
       max(created_at) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York' AS last_edt
FROM harness_shared.memory_recall_stats
WHERE created_at > now() - interval '8 hours'
GROUP BY surface ORDER BY n DESC;
```

Columns are `hit_count` / `top_score` (NOT `hits`). Expected-active surfaces on
a busy fleet: `search`, `initialize`, `claim`, `create`, `compact`, `brief` —
plus `orient` and `turn-start` once those paths are healthy (both were the
silent/broken ones found 2026-07-12). ⚠ Liveness by COUNT alone can mask a
whole population getting nothing: 68 initialize recalls/8h looked healthy while
every one belonged to a stateless client and zero reached a real agent —
always cross-check the ledger's identity kinds (below).

## The score-scale trap (criteria: admission-floor-integrity + the orient fold)

The hybrid backend returns **reciprocal-rank-fusion scores**: rank-1 on one leg
≈ `1/61 ≈ 0.0164`, on both legs ≈ `0.0328`. Pure-vector paths return cosine
(≈0.5–0.9). A floor calibrated for one scale silently zeroes the other — the
2026-07-12 live incident: orient's blanket 0.05 floor emptied every fold
(`hits: [], filteredLowScore: 5`) while `search`'s p50 looked fine. When a
surface's `top_score` p50 sits near 0.016–0.033, that is the RRF signature,
not "bad memories."

## Dedup-ledger identity (criterion: dedup-ledger-integrity)

```sql
SELECT CASE WHEN session_id LIKE 's-%' THEN 'synthetic s-*'
            WHEN session_id LIKE 'su-%' THEN 'su ownerId'
            ELSE 'other' END AS id_kind,
       port, count(DISTINCT session_id) AS sessions, count(*) AS rows
FROM harness_shared.memory_session_surfaced
WHERE surfaced_at > now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1;
```

The invariant: ONE identity per session across every port — the MCP URL's
`client=` (from `PAPERCUSP_SID`) == the hook owner == the coord ownerId. The
`s-*` shape is the transport-id fallback for clients that supplied no
`client=`; a port whose stamps are predominantly `s-*`/`other` while agent
sessions run is the "identity drift — one end renamed" marker live (this exact
query found initialize fully drifted on 2026-07-12; root cause: the psu MCP URL
template lacked `&harness=`, fixed in `claude-integration.ts`).

Epoch semantics: `bumpSessionEpoch` fires once per compaction via the
recovery-brief endpoint; the re-prime stamps the NEW epoch under
`port='compact'`. Same memory_id under two ports in ONE epoch = the
double-injection signature. ⚠ Forensics: read the ledger DURING a drill —
superseded-epoch rows persist only until the 14-day age sweep (and were
bump-deleted before 2026-07-12).

## Live end-to-end probe (the drill-2 protocol, replayable)

Plant two harness-scoped fixture memories (record ids), launch one visible
subject on a plan that requires: (A) report fixture-fact-1 at session start
stating the delivery source first; (B) `session:request-compaction` while
holding the WI, with a focus that forbids carrying the values; (C) report
fixture-fact-2 post-compaction, delivery source first. Grade delivery from the
ledger (initialize/claim stamps pre-compaction; epoch+1 `compact` stamps after)
and consumption from the completion record. Cleanup: `memory:forget` both ids
(they leak into other agents' folds while they exist), wind down the fleet.
Full worked example: plan `recall-drill-2-injection-2026-07-12` + scorecards
EI-10406/EI-10407.
